'''Carli Renzi''' (born 24 October 1982) is an Australian judo competitor and wrestler.  She represented Australia in wrestling at the [[2010 Commonwealth Games]] and the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] in judo in the 52 – 57&nbsp;kg&nbsp;— Women event.

==Personal life==
Nicknamed Carli, Renzi was born on 24 October 1982 in [[East Melbourne, Victoria]]. She attended St Mary's Primary School, Greensborough  before going to [[Eltham College (Victoria)|Eltham College]].  She then attended [[Deakin University]] from 2001 to 2005 where she earned a Bachelor of Commerce with Honours in Finance. {{As of|2012}}, she lives in Melbourne, Victoria. While Renzi is primarily a judo and wrestling competitor, other sport disciplines she is involved with include [[Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu]], a sport she took up to help her gain Olympic selection. Renzi is {{convert|167|cm}} tall and weighs {{convert|57|kg}}.<ref name=aoc>{{cite web|url=http://london2012.olympics.com.au/athlete/carli-renzi |title=London 2012 - Carli Renzi |publisher=Australian Olympic Committee |date=1982-10-24 |accessdate=2012-07-08}}</ref>

==Wrestling==
Renzi started wrestling in 2007. She represented Australia at the [[2010 Commonwealth Games]] in [[Wrestling at the 2010 Commonwealth Games – Women's freestyle 59 kg|free-style wrestling]], finishing sixth in the U/59&nbsp;kg division.<ref name=aoc/><ref name=knockedout>{{cite web|author=Jim Morton |url=http://news.smh.com.au/breaking-news-sport/wrestler-farzad-paving-way-for-brother-20101008-16bn6.html |title=Wrestler Farzad paving way for brother |publisher=Sydney Morning Herald |date=2010-10-08 |accessdate=2012-07-08}}</ref><ref name=askquestion>{{cite web |url=http://wwos.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=8100370 |title=Mud or jelly? Not likely |publisher=Nine MSN |accessdate=2012-07-08 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121230181833/http://wwos.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=8100370 |archive-date=30 December 2012 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>  Frequently, when men found out Renzi was a wrestler, they asked her if she did mud or jelly wrestling. Going into the 2010 Commonwealth Games, she trained with [[Emily Bensted]].  People at Renzi's place of employment did not believe she was going to the Commonwealth Games to compete in the sport.<ref name="askquestion"/><ref name=quoteofgames>{{cite web|url=http://au.sports.yahoo.com/commonwealth-games/galleries/photo/8141150/quotes-of-the-delhi-games/8141471/ |title=Quotes of the Delhi Games Delhi 2010 |publisher=Yahoo!7 Sport |date=2010-10-15 |accessdate=2012-07-08 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101020134657/http://au.sports.yahoo.com/commonwealth-games/galleries/photo/8141150/quotes-of-the-delhi-games/8141471/ |archivedate=20 October 2010 |df=dmy }}</ref>

==Judo==
Renzi started in the sport when she was seven years old and initially fought against boys in the mixed U/20&nbsp;kg division.  She is a member of Dominance Mixed Martial Arts and has a judo scholarship with the Australian Institute of Sport. She was coached by Daniel Kelly and Maria Pekli since 2003. Her primary training base is in Melbourne, with a secondary training base in Canberra.<ref name=aoc/>

At the [[Australian National Judo Championships|Australian Championships]] in the 2005, 2006, 2007, 2011 and 2012 Renzi took home gold. She finished 9th in the U/57&nbsp;kg category at the 2011 Tokyo Grand Slam in Tokyo, Japan. She finished 2nd in the U/57&nbsp;kg category at the 2011 Apia World Cup in Apia, Western Samoa. She finished 3rd  in the U/57&nbsp;kg category at the 2011 US Open in Miami. She finished 1st in the U/57&nbsp;kg category at the 2012 Oceania Championships in Cairns, Australia. She finished 9th in the U/57&nbsp;kg category at the 2012 Budapest World Cup event in Budapest, Hungary.{{citation needed|date=August 2012}} She was selected to represent [[Australia at the 2012 Summer Olympics|Australia]] at the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] in judo in the 52 – 57&nbsp;kg&nbsp;— Women event.<ref name=source1>{{cite web|url=http://www.portlincolntimes.com.au/news/local/sport/martial-arts/judo-takes-jake-to-olympics/2595408.aspx |title=Judo takes Jake to Olympics - Local News - Sport - Martial Arts |publisher=Port Lincoln Times |date=2012-06-18 |accessdate=2012-07-08}}</ref> The Games were her first.<ref name=aoc/><ref name=source32>{{cite web|author=H1 |url=http://nz.sports.yahoo.com/news/article/-/14016808/dos-santos-experience-corner/ |title=Dos Santos has experience in his corner |publisher=Yahoo! New Zealand Sport |date=2012-06-22 |accessdate=2012-07-08 }}{{dead link|date=November 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name=source34>{{cite web |url=http://wwos.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=8488128 |title=Dos Santos has experience in his corner |publisher=Nine MSN |accessdate=2012-07-08 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121230125052/http://wwos.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=8488128 |archive-date=30 December 2012 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>  She reached the third round, losing to eventual bronze medalist, [[Automne Pavia]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = 52 - 57kg (lightweight) women results - Judo - London 2012 Olympics|url = http://www.olympic.org/olympic-results/london-2012/judo/52-57kg-lightweight-w|website = www.olympic.org|accessdate = 2015-04-26}}</ref>
